registeredBy: the item-quality harness builder (branch feat/item-eval), before any rating
note: The blind rubric for generated flashcards and quiz items (measurement plan MS4 'human-rated rubric'). Raters see items with no system name, no source quote and one normalised format; the key to which system wrote which item is sealed until scoring. Each dimension is an ordinal 1-4 scale; 'na' only where the dimension says so.

dimensions.question: Is the item correct according to the course material given as the reference?

anchors.1: Wrong: the keyed answer contradicts the reference, or more than one answer is right.
anchors.2: Partly wrong or ambiguous: a careful student could defend another answer.
anchors.3: Correct, with a minor imprecision that would not mislead.
anchors.4: Correct and exactly as the reference states it.

dimensions.question: Can a student tell exactly what is asked and what counts as the answer?

anchors.2: Answerable, but wording, blank placement or format gets in the way.

dimensions.question: Does the item test something this course would plausibly assess, rather than trivia from the material?

anchors.1: Trivia or incidental detail (a speaker's aside, a page artefact).
anchors.4: A central concept or skill of the course.

dimensions.question: Is the difficulty right for a student preparing for this course's exam (not a giveaway, not beyond the material)?

anchors.1: A giveaway (the answer is visible or guessable from the wording) or beyond the material.
anchors.2: Too easy or too hard for the course level.
anchors.4: Well pitched: requires the knowledge the course teaches.

dimensions.question: Multiple choice only: are the wrong options plausible to a student who has not learned the idea, and clearly wrong to one who has?

anchors.1: Implausible or off-topic distractors, or a distractor is also right.
anchors.2: One or more distractors are obviously wrong (length, form or topic gives them away).
anchors.4: All plausible, same form and length as the key, each clearly wrong.

pairwise.question: Which of the two items would better prepare a student for this course's exam? Answer A, B or tie.
pairwise.orderSwap: Every pair is presented twice, once in each order, in separately shuffled positions. A pair counts toward a preference only when both presentations agree (Zheng et al. 2023, arXiv 2306.05685: position bias; swap consistency is reported).

rules: An LLM rater must be a different model family from every generator whose items are in the set (measurement plan MT4); the scorer refuses otherwise.
Rate against the reference material, not general knowledge (reference-guided judging; Zheng et al. 2023 reports it cut wrong 'correct' math verdicts from 14 of 20 to 3 of 20).
Math and numeric items: the harness's code recomputation is the reference for the value; the rater judges wording and relevance.
Never open the sealed folder before scoring.
raters.agreement: With two raters on overlapping tasks: quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa per ordinal dimension (never pooled across dimensions), Cohen's kappa for the pairwise verdict. With rotating raters or missing ratings, switch to Krippendorff's alpha (not implemented here).
